extraction.author: Supply Chain Engineering, Wide World Importers

functional_requirements.text: Calculate demand forecasts using 24 months of historical sales data per SKU
Generate automated purchase orders when inventory falls below configurable reorder point
Support inter-warehouse stock transfers with approval workflow (single-level < $10K, dual-level ≥ $10K)
Real-time inventory visibility across all 8 warehouses via unified dashboard
Barcode and RFID scanning for receiving, picking, and shipping operations
Calculate optimal safety stock levels per SKU per warehouse (default service level: 95%)
Integrate with SAP S/4HANA for financial posting of inventory movements
Lot tracking and expiry date management for perishable goods
Mobile-optimized interfaces for warehouse floor operations

non_functional_requirements.text: Dashboard load within 3 seconds for up to 50,000 SKUs
Forecast calculations complete within 15 minutes for ~12,000 active SKUs
99.5% availability during business hours (6 AM – 10 PM local warehouse time)
OAuth 2.0 authentication and RBAC with warehouse-level scoping

acceptance_criteria.criterion: PO auto-generated within 5 min of threshold
Dashboard shows data from all 8 warehouses
Safety stock within 10% of analytical solution
SAP posting verified in test environment

dependencies: ML Platform for demand forecasting models (Azure ML)
standards_references: ISO 22742 (Linear bar code and two-dimensional symbols)
SOC 2 Type II (AICPA Trust Services Criteria)
assumptions_constraints: SAP S/4HANA APIs available in test environment by March 2026
Historical sales data (24 months) cleansed and available in data warehouse
RFID readers installed at all warehouse dock doors
Phase 2 must not modify Phase 1 database schema (additive only)
No open-source ML frameworks without security review approval

glossary.definition: Stock Keeping Unit — unique product identifier
Mean Absolute Percentage Error — forecast accuracy metric
Buffer inventory to protect against demand variability
Inventory level that triggers a replenishment order

areas.notes: 10 FRs covering forecasting, automation, multi-warehouse, scanning, and integration
7 NFRs with measurable targets; could add more on data integrity and error handling
SOC 2 + OAuth 2.0 + RBAC is solid; missing data encryption requirements
Acceptance criteria provided for 8 of 17 requirements; FR-105, FR-108, FR-109, FR-110 lack criteria
GS1, ISO 22742, SOC 2 referenced; relevant for warehouse/inventory domain

recommendations: FR-105 (barcode/RFID), FR-108 (lot tracking), FR-109 (ABC reports), FR-110 (mobile UI) lack acceptance criteria — define measurable pass/fail conditions
No data encryption requirements specified — add at-rest and in-transit encryption NFRs given SOC 2 compliance target
No explicit error handling or failure recovery requirements — define behavior for SAP integration failures, ML model failures, and scanner disconnections
Additive-only schema constraint may limit forecasting model flexibility — consider documenting the migration path if schema changes become necessary
$350K budget for 10 FRs including SAP integration and ML forecasting is aggressive — SAP integration alone typically requires $100K–$200K
